title: Advanced Spelling Conventions
keyIdea: Three Year 5 and 6 spelling rules depend on what you hear. When you add a vowel ending to a word ending in -fer, double the r only if -fer is still stressed: referring and preferred, but reference and preference. For the ee sound, write i before e except after c: believe and chief, but receive and ceiling; science keeps ie because it has no ee sound. The letter string ough makes several sounds, as in thought, rough, cough, though, through and plough, so each ough word has to be learned by sound as well as sight.
familyTip: Say a -fer word with an ending, like referring or reference, and clap the loud beat together. Is the loud beat on -fer? Then the r doubles. On a walk or in a book, hunt for ough words and say them aloud: how many different sounds can you find?

visual.caption: Double r or one r? Drag each word, or tap it and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap the stressed beat, build -fer words, fill ie or ei gaps, sort ough words by sound, then proofread a note.

kid: Some spellings depend on what you hear, not just what you see. So say the word out loud first. Listen for the loud beat. That loud beat is called the stress.

Look at words that end in -fer, like refer and prefer. When you add an ending that starts with a vowel, listen to the -fer. Do you still say -FER loudly? Then double the r: re-FER-ring, pre-FERRED. Has the stress moved to the front? Then keep one r: REF-er-ence, PREF-er-ence.

Next, ie and ei. For the ee sound, it is i before e, except after c. So we write believe and chief, but receive and ceiling. The rule is only for the ee sound. In science and ancient you do not say ee, so they keep ie.

Last, ough. These four letters can say many sounds. Thought rhymes with saw. Rough rhymes with stuff. Cough says off. Though says oh. Through says oo. Plough rhymes with cow. Learn each one by how it sounds as well as how it looks.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. These are statutory Years 5 and 6 spelling rules in English Appendix 1 of the National Curriculum in England: adding suffixes beginning with vowel letters to words ending in -fer (the r doubles if -fer is still stressed: referring, referred, referral, preferring, preferred; it stays single if not: reference, referee, preference); the /iː/ sound spelt ei after c (deceive, receive, ceiling, with exceptions protein, caffeine and seize); and the letter string ough. Hyphens after prefixes such as re-enter are covered in a separate lesson.

The lab has five tasks. Learners tap the stressed syllable in six words and see the stress move between refer and reference. They build six -fer words and the syllable strip shows why the r doubles or not. They fill six ie or ei gaps, including science, sort ten ough words into six sound groups, and finally proofread a short note with three slips and three tempting correct words.

Common mistakes. Children double the r in every -fer word (preferrence) or never (prefered), because they look at the letters instead of listening for the stress. Many apply i before e except after c to every ie word and write sceince, or miss that the rule is only for the ee sound. Others assume ough words that look alike must rhyme, so though and through get the same sound.

practice.hint: Say it aloud. Is -fer still the loud beat?
practice.explain: You say re-FER-ring, so -fer is still stressed and the r doubles: referring.

practice.prompt: Fill the gap: c__ling (the top of a room).
practice.hint: The gap comes straight after c and makes an ee sound.
practice.explain: After c, the ee sound is spelt ei: ceiling.

practice.prompt: A -fer word has {n} letters, like refer. You add -ing and -fer is still stressed. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: Count the extra r as well as the letters of ing.
practice.explain: The r doubles (1 more letter) and ing adds 3, so {n} + 1 + 3 = {=n+4} letters (refer 5 → referring 9).

practice.hint: Say it aloud. Where is the loud beat now?
practice.explain: You say PREF-er-ence. The stress moved off -fer, so keep one r: preference.

practice.prompt: A -fer word has {n} letters, like prefer. You add -ed and say pre-FERRED. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: Is -fer still stressed? Then the r doubles before ed.
practice.explain: The r doubles (1 more letter) and ed adds 2, so {n} + 1 + 2 = {=n+3} letters (prefer 6 → preferred 9).

pool.prompt: transfer + ed. Which spelling is right?
pool.hint: Say trans-fer-red. Which beat is loud?
pool.explain: You say trans-FER-red, so -fer stays stressed and the r doubles: transferred.

pool.prompt: Which spelling of the word meaning “to get” is right?
pool.hint: The ee sound comes straight after c.
pool.explain: After c, the ee sound is spelt ei: receive, like ceiling and deceive.

pool.prompt: Which word has ough rhyming with cow?
pool.hint: Say each word aloud and listen for the ow sound.
pool.explain: Plough rhymes with cow. Cough says off and dough says oh.

pool.prompt: confer + ence. Which spelling is right?
pool.hint: Say it aloud. Where is the stress?
pool.explain: You say CON-fer-ence, so -fer is not stressed and the r stays single.

pool.hint: Is there a c before the ee sound?
pool.explain: No c comes before the ee sound, so it is i before e: believe.

pool.prompt: Jo spells “referal”. What is the slip?
choices: -fer is still stressed, so it needs rr: referral
pool.hint: Say re-fer-ral. Which beat is loud?
pool.explain: You say re-FER-ral, so the r doubles: referral.

pool.prompt: Which pair of ough words rhyme?
pool.hint: Say them aloud. Do not trust the letters.
pool.explain: Bought and thought both say or. Though says oh but through says oo; rough says uff but dough says oh.

pool.prompt: Which word breaks the ei-after-c rule on purpose, because it has no ee sound?
pool.hint: Which word does not have an ee sound after c?
pool.explain: In ancient the c and i make a sh sound, with no ee, so the rule does not apply.

pool.prompt: Which word has ough saying oh?
pool.hint: Say each word. Which one rhymes with go?
pool.explain: Though rhymes with go. Through says oo and rough says uff.

pool.prompt: Why is science spelt with ie after c?
choices: It has no ee sound there
pool.hint: Which sound is the ei-after-c rule about?
pool.explain: The rule is only for the ee sound. In science you say sigh-ence, so it is ie.

pool.prompt: A -fer word has {n} letters, like confer. You add -ence and say CON-fer-ence. How many letters does the new word have?
pool.hint: The stress moved off -fer, so does the r double?
pool.explain: The stress moved, so the r stays single. Ence adds 4 letters: {n} + 4 = {=n+4} (confer 6 → conference 10).

pool.prompt: A -fer word has {n} letters, like refer. You add -al and still say re-FER-ral. How many letters does the new word have?
pool.hint: -fer is still stressed, so count the extra r too.
pool.explain: The r doubles (1 more letter) and al adds 2, so {n} + 1 + 2 = {=n+3} letters (refer 5 → referral 8).
